subject: Clarify training rights & data sovereignty - redlines
messages:
From: Becca Li <becca.li@horizon.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@novum.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify training rights & data sovereignty - Horizon MSA redlines

Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our legal team attached a redlined MSA that has two major asks we need explicit language on before procurement can move forward:

1) Training & feedback license: they want an explicit opt-out (no rights granted) so Horizon's customer content and telemetry are never used to improve models or for derivative training.
2) Data sovereignty: EU-sourced content must remain within EU infrastructure; they want a contractual guarantee plus an appendix listing processing locations and audit options.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these carveouts as written, or propose alternative language that preserves our ability to run platform improvements (telemetry, bug fixes) but not incorporate raw customer content into model training?

Attached: Horizon_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx (redlines), Data_Sovereignty_Appendix.pdf

We have a procurement deadline of June 30. Appreciate a quick response so we can surface to our CPO.

Best,
Becca Li
Senior Counsel, Horizon Analytics

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Becca Li <becca.li@horizon.ai>
Cc: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@novum.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify training rights & data sovereignty - Horizon MSA redlines

Becca —

Thanks for sending this over and flagging the deadline. We reviewed the redlines and summarized our position below. I attached a working redline (Redlines_MSA_v3.docx) that tries to bridge the gap and keeps commercial guardrails intact.

Summary of proposed approach (high-level):
- Training/Feedback: We can accept a strong customer opt-out for using raw customer content for model re-training and long-term model improvement. In exchange we propose a narrow carve-in that allows Redwood to use aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics for platform stability, latency improvements, and bug fixes. We added explicit definitions for "anonymized telemetry" and a prohibition on using customer PII for model training.
- Data sovereignty: We will commit to processing EU-personal-data in EU-only infrastructure for any data marked by you as EU-sourced. We propose a Data Sovereignty Appendix (see attached) that lists regions, subprocessors, and audit windows. For audit, we can provide SOC2 extracts and scoped logs; for deeper audits we propose a negotiated cost-based process.

Open items where Legal signoff is needed:
- Wording around "anonymized telemetry" (Connor, see section 4.2 in Redlines_MSA_v3) — legal needs to confirm sufficiency and whether we should add a cryptographic irreversibility clause.
- The retention carveouts if Horizon opts-out of training — operations needs a clear retention/exports path to avoid indefinite KV cache growth.
- Consequences for cross-border fallback: we proposed a limited fallback where if EU capacity is unavailable, requests will fail rather than route to non-EU regions. Confirm this risk appetite.

Attachments: Redlines_MSA_v3.docx (proposed compromise), Data_Sovereignty_Appendix.pdf

If acceptable I can push this to procurement as a counterproposal — otherwise please flag specific language you cannot accept.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0199

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify training rights & data sovereignty - Horizon MSA redlines

Kimberly —

Thanks for the ping and the working redline. Quick legal read-through and comments below (I attached an annotated PDF in the Drive link).

1) Anonymized telemetry (section 4.2) — we should tighten the definition. Replace the current clause with: "Anonymized Telemetry means aggregated metrics and telemetry that cannot be re-associated with an identifiable natural person or account, where irreversible hashing or differential privacy techniques have been applied." Add an explicit exclusion: "Anonymized Telemetry excludes any data elements that, alone or in combination, constitute Personal Data as defined under GDPR." That gives both legal clarity and operational constraints.

2) Training opt-out mechanics — we can accept an opt-out but must limit the scope to:
   - No training on raw customer content or customer-specific fine-tuning datasets.
   - Redwood may continue to use operational logs and aggregate metrics for platform reliability and model performance metrics that are not traceable to a customer.
   - If Horizon opts out, add a 90-day transition period for existing cached state and a documented deletion/export plan. (See retention language I proposed.)

3) Data sovereignty & fallback — accept EU-only processing as requested, but include an emergency exception clause: "In the event of prolonged EU-region outage preventing service availability for > 4 hours, requests may be routed to alternative regions as a temporary failover subject to encryption-in-transit and notification requirements." Horizon may reject failover — if so we'll need to accept a higher availability risk and price accordingly.

4) Audit requests — offer SOC2 extracts and logs as first-tier; for full on-site or detailed forensics, we propose a scoped, cost-recoverable engagement. Add a standard response SLA (10 business days) for producing audit materials.

If you want I can convert these bullets into exact contract language and drop them into Redlines_MSA_v3.docx. Laura — PTAL on retention/export plan for opt-out so we can include the practical steps.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
